chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the Aqeeqa for the newborn, how it is? He said: When seven days come upon the newborn, name him by the name that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has named him with. Then shave his head, and give in charity the weight of his hair in gold or silver, and slaughter a ram for him. And if a ram is not found, suffice it with whatever suffices in the Udhiyah (Qurbani), or else a lamb, the largest of the lambs of the year. And give the midwife a quarter of it. And if there is no midwife, it is for his mother; she gives it to whomever she wishes, and feeds from it ten of the Muslims. If they increase, that is better, and eat from it.

And the Aqeeqa is obligatory whether one is rich or poor, when one is able. And if one does not perform the Aqeeqa for him until he performs the Udhiyah for him, then the Udhiyah suffices for him. And he said: If the midwife is a Jewess, who does not eat from the slaughter of the Muslims, she is given the value of a quarter of the ram.

key_terms.الْأُضْحِيَّة: Udhiyah: The sacrifice offered during Eid al-Adha
key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةُ: Aqeeqa: The sacrifice made for a newborn child on the seventh day
key_terms.رُبُعُهَا: A quarter of the sacrificed animal

ai.seo_question: What are the steps and rulings for performing Aqeeqa for a newborn in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Aqeeqa as a recommended act (mustahabb) that becomes obligatory upon wealth accumulation, detailing the specific rituals of naming, shaving, and sacrificing a ram on the seventh day. It provides practical jurisprudential nuances, such as substituting a lamb if a ram is unavailable and adjusting compensation for non-Muslim midwives, reflecting the flexibility within Shia fiqh. The text underscores the social dimension of the ritual by mandating the distribution of meat to ten Muslims, thereby fostering community bonds alongside the spiritual act of gratitude.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Bin Musa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked himasws about the Aqeeqa from the new-born, how it is (to be done)?’ Heasws said: ‘When seven days come upon the new-born, name by the name Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has Named it by, then shave off his head, and give in charity by the weight of his hair, gold or silver, and slaughter a ram from him, and a ram cannot be found, suffice it with whatever it is sufficed by during the slaughtering, or else bear a lamb what happens to be the best of the lambs a year old, and give the midwife a quarter; and if there does not happen to be a midwife, so it is up to its mother to give to whomsoever she so desires to, and feed from it ten from the Muslims. So it you can increase, so it is better; and eat from it.

And the Aqeeqa is necessary whether one is rich or poor, when it is easier, even if one has not performed Aqeeqa from it, even of a sacrifice from it, so the slaughter would suffice for it’. And heasws said: ‘If the mid-wife was a Jewess, not eating from the slaughter of the Muslims, give to her the price of a quarter of the ram’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ali from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amir ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about ‘Aqiqah and a newborn. He (the Imam) has stated this Hadith. ‘When a child is seven days old a name with which Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has named him must be given to him, then his head must be shaved and equal to the weight of his hairs gold or silver should be given in charity. A ram should be slaughtered, and if a ram is not available then whatever is sufficient for an animal offering during al-Hajj is sufficient for ‘Aqiqah. If this is not available then a lamb of the same year is sufficient. Al-Qabilah (the special nurse, doctor) should be given one-fourth of the meat thereof. If there is no al-Qabilah then it is up to the mother to whomever she wants to give and ten Muslims should be fed. If there are more than ten it is better. ‘Aqiqah is obligatory if one is affluent or even if one is poor; he must do so when he is able to manage; and if ‘Aqiqah is not done for one until he offers an offering animal during al-Hajj, it then is sufficient for ‘Aqiqah.’

He (the Imam) then said, ‘If al-Qabilah (the special nurse, doctor) is a Jewish woman who does not eat meat of the animal slaughtered by Muslims then one-fourth of the price of the animal for ‘Aqiqah should be given to her.’”
